form_analysis.feedback: Exceptional aftercare form specifically for CO₂ laser resurfacing with detailed guidance on this gold-standard treatment. Comprehensive coverage of the unique CO₂ healing phases, frosting management, and prolonged erythema. Strong emphasis on the extended recovery timeline and hyperpigmentation prevention.

form_data.introduction: This aftercare is specifically for CO₂ LASER resurfacing (10,600nm wavelength). CO₂ laser vaporizes tissue with extreme precision and significant thermal effect. The gold standard for dramatic resurfacing but requires extensive, meticulous aftercare.

instructions.general_directive: Follow for 10-21 days of intensive care, with 3-6 months of sun protection and ongoing management. CO₂ has unique healing characteristics.

sections.title: CO₂ Laser Specifics
sections.content: 10,600nm wavelength absorbed by water in tissue. Creates: 1) Immediate tissue vaporization 2) Significant thermal coagulation zone 3) Prolonged inflammatory response for collagen stimulation.

sections.title: Frosting & Immediate Response
items: FROSTING: White, chalky appearance immediately after - indicates tissue dehydration/vaporization.

sections.title: CO₂ Healing Phases (Extended)
items: Days 0-7: Open wound phase. Constant ointment application critical.
Days 7-14: Re-epithelialization. Itching intense. Crust formation.
Weeks 2-6: Pink phase. Skin delicate, shiny. Prone to milia.
Months 2-6: Redness gradually fades. Final results emerge.

sections.title: Prolonged Erythema Management
sections.content: CO₂ causes SIGNIFICANT prolonged redness (3-6 months). Manage with: 1) Green color corrector makeup after 3 weeks 2) IPL treatments for residual redness after 3 months 3) Avoidance of all irritants.

sections.title: Hyperpigmentation Prevention (CRITICAL)
sections.content: CO₂-treated skin is HIGHLY prone to post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation, especially in darker skin types. PREVENTION: 1) Strict sun avoidance for 6+ months 2) Hydroquinone or other lighteners after 4 weeks 3) Antioxidant protection.

sections.title: Milial Management
sections.content: CO₂ commonly causes milia (tiny white bumps) during healing. DO NOT PICK. They will resolve with gentle exfoliation after 6-8 weeks. Your practitioner can extract if persistent.

sections.title: Realistic CO₂ Expectations
items: Downtime: 10-21 days social, 3-6 months for redness.
One treatment often sufficient for dramatic change.
Not recommended for Fitzpatrick IV-VI without extreme caution.
